Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
MU 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 quantity of X What happens to the total utility as consumption of X rises from 1 to 6 units?

options.A: It falls continuously.
options.B: It falls and then rises.
options.C: It rises continuously.
options.D: It rises and then falls.

questions.questionText: An indifference curve is typically drawn with a convex shape. Which economic concept explains the reason for this convex shape?

options.A: allocative efficiency
options.B: diminishing marginal rate of substitution
options.C: Pareto optimality
options.D: the equi-marginal principle

questions.questionText: What is most likely to increase the principal–agent problem?

options.A: ensuring the actions of agents are known by the managers
options.B: linking the rewards of managers with the profitability of the firm
options.C: removing from managers the opportunity to hold shares
options.D: preparing contracts that compel agents to work in the interest of the principal

questions.questionText: 1000 6000 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Average fixed cost falls.
options.B: Average fixed cost is constant.
options.C: Average variable cost falls.
options.D: Average variable cost rises.

questions.questionText: Which condition is necessary for a firm to practise third degree price discrimination effectively?

options.A: All consumers and producers must be in the same geographical location.
options.B: Customers must be divided into separate markets for the same product.
options.C: Each separate market must have identical price elasticities of demand.
options.D: Price undercutting is required to enter a monopolistic market.

questions.questionText: A traffic study concluded that there would be significant benefits if 10% of car drivers switched to using motorcycles during peak traffic times. Which benefit of this change would be considered a private benefit?

options.A: faster journeys for those who continued to go by car
options.B: faster journeys for those who switched to motorcycles
options.C: increased safety for cyclists
options.D: reduced levels of air pollution for pedestrians

questions.questionText: Which conditions are most likely to reduce the accuracy of cost-benefit analysis in decision making? proportion of external % of total costs and costs and benefits to total benefits that are in total costs and benefits the future

options.A: high high
options.B: high low
options.C: low high
options.D: low low

questions.questionText: What is consistent with a movement towards Pareto optimality?

options.A: when negative externality lowers the utility of an individual
options.B: when consumption of a good is non-rival
options.C: when reallocation of resources can make someone better off without making any other person worse off
options.D: when trade takes place to make one nation better off at the expense of its trading partner

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the short-run supply curve and long-run supply curve of labour. short run wage rate long run X Y Z D O quantity of labour Which area turns from economic rent in the short run to transfer earnings in the long run?

options.A: X B X + Y C Y D Y + Z

questions.questionText: Which policies might a government introduce to increase the marginal productivity of labour? tax allowances better for capital education goods

options.A: no no
options.B: no yes
options.C: yes no
options.D: yes yes

questions.questionText: What is most likely to increase relative poverty in a country?

options.A: increasing means-tested benefit levels
options.B: increasing the power of trade unions
options.C: making the tax system more progressive
options.D: removing the national minimum wage

questions.questionText: Which policy is not designed to correct a market failure?

options.A: government provision of healthcare
options.B: price controls on large firms
options.C: regulations to limit smoke pollution
options.D: introducing import quotas

questions.questionText: To control the cost of living, governments have sometimes imposed a maximum price on certain goods that is below the free market price. What is often an undesirable side effect of such a policy?

options.A: accelerating general inflation
options.B: an increase in profits above normal profits
options.C: an increase in the stocks of unsold goods held by firms
options.D: shortages of the good

questions.questionText: When is an increase in national income most likely to induce an increase in investment spending?

options.A: when firms have spare production capacity
options.B: when firms use labour-intensive production
options.C: when the increase in income is regarded as permanent
options.D: when the increase in income is regarded as temporary

questions.questionText: What is a function of money?

options.A: It can be divided into small units.
options.B: It can be easily carried.
options.C: It is a standard of deferred payment.
options.D: It is widely accepted.

questions.questionText: A pandemic encourages many workers in developed countries to work from home, leading to a closure of city centre businesses such as coffee shops and retailers. If this way of working continues after the pandemic, what is the most likely result?

options.A: Frictional unemployment will decrease.
options.B: The geographical mobility of labour will increase.
options.C: Structural unemployment will increase.
options.D: Voluntary unemployment will increase.

questions.questionText: In its 2020 population census, China reported that the total population was just below 1.4 billion. The birth rate had continued to decline, the number of those reaching retirement age had increased and the percentage size of the workforce had decreased. Which change of policy would most quickly sustain China’s economic growth in view of these population changes?

options.A: Allow more immigration of labour.
options.B: Encourage women to leave work to have more children.
options.C: Increase research in technology to improve labour productivity.
options.D: Tax the labour force more to pay for the increasing number of pensions.

questions.questionText: Other things remaining equal, what will reduce the level of national income in an economy?

options.A: a fall in planned savings
options.B: a fall in the marginal propensity to import
options.C: an increase in the average propensity to consume
options.D: a reduction in the level of defence expenditure

questions.questionText: What, according to the accelerator principle, will cause the level of investment to fall?

options.A: a decrease in confidence
options.B: a decrease in the rate of growth of national income
options.C: an increase in the price of capital equipment
options.D: an increase in the rate of interest

questions.questionText: What is measured on the vertical axis of the Phillips curve?

options.A: the rate of change of real wages
options.B: the rate of change of take-home pay
options.C: the rate of inflation
options.D: the rate of interest

questions.questionText: Which change would be most likely to indicate that a country has experienced economic development?

options.A: an appreciation in the country’s currency
options.B: an improvement in the average citizen’s quality of life
options.C: an improvement in the country’s trade balance
options.D: an increase in the country’s real GDP

questions.questionText: The table gives some economic indicators for four countries. Which country is closest to achieving the principal aims of government economic policy? balance of change in GDP rate of inflation unemployment payments (%) (%) (%) (% of GDP)
What is a government macroeconomic aim?

options.A: a fall in the general price level of goods and services
options.B: an increase in monopoly regulation
options.C: lower taxes on consumer goods
options.D: a minimum wage for low paid agricultural workers

questions.questionText: Which row correctly identifies the characteristics of a low-income economy? dependency Gini coefficient per capita on the primary value real income sector

options.A: high high high
options.B: high high low
options.C: high low low
options.D: low high low

questions.questionText: What is the role of the International Monetary Fund (IMF)?

options.A: to advise countries that are experiencing trade disagreements
options.B: to help charities providing emergency assistance to countries in need
options.C: to offer short-term assistance to countries with balance of payments problems
options.D: to provide interest-free credit to developing countries for infrastructure purposes
